analyst_view.overall: Early view: AGF are still looking for a first league-phase win (lost 1-0 at Gent, 1-1 with Egnatia, 0-0 with Braga), while John van den Brom's Twente have won all three (1-0 Thun, 4-1 Lincoln, 3-1 Pafos). Twente need the points to stay in the top eight, AGF need them to get into the top 24. No injury news for this game yet; it is refreshed with team news the day before.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean a little lower: AGF have scored two goals in three European games and kept Braga out in a 0-0, and Twente dominated possession against Pafos but struggled to create in the first half before winning 3-1 against ten men.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, with Twente taking most of them. Twente's control of the ball should push AGF back and win corners, which fits the estimate, so I stay with it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. Nothing in the news points to a heated game or a strict referee yet; the referee is not known, so I stay with the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.6 shots, nearly 23 of them from Twente. That is a lot for an away side; Twente's first half against Pafos was slow for clear chances and AGF created the better first-half openings against Braga, so I lean a bit lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. AGF goalkeeper Mads Hedenstad was busy against Braga and Twente have Wout Weghorst and Daouda Weidmann testing keepers, so I see no reason to move off the estimate.
